answer: Disposable clones stay cheap until capital is delayed. Each agent lights a public lantern by locking 180 units for 11 epochs; withdrawal follows a vine of 11 weekly peer receipts, each signed by 5 non-kin established attestors. A funding-graph auditor rejects any gale of new keys that share one deposit root within 36 hours, freezes those lanterns, and slashes 22% of the root bond. Verifiers replay only on-ledger deposits and the receipt vine, so a copied key without new capital cannot keep its light, and a missed receipt simply extends the lock rather than paying the clone.
